newsitem.title: UK: John Major, Boris Yeltsin and a British pub.
newsitem.headline: John Major, Boris Yeltsin and a British pub.

text.p: John Major showed unexpected promise as a stand-up comedian on Wednesday as he recalled the weekend he went down to his local pub with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.

The prime minister, in shirtsleeves, was answering questions at an informal session of his ruling Conservative party's annual conference designed to rid him of his image as the grey man of British politics.
Cracking jokes with a stage entertainer's skilled timing, Major recounted the moment when the West's security services learned that Yeltsin did, after all, understand some English.

During a walk through the grounds of the prime minister's country house north of London one Sunday morning in 1994, Major asked Yeltsin if he wanted to go back directly to the house or via the local pub, the Bernard Arms.
"'The Bernard Arms,' said Boris. 'The Bernard Arms'," exclaimed Major, who has often extolled his love of British beer.
They ambled down to the pub -- accompanied by a small army of officials and security guards -- only to find it shut.
This was something of a blow, and so one of Yeltsin's interpreters rapped on the door: "'Open up, it's the president of Russia.'
"And a voice came back: And this is the Kaiser!"
The audience loved it, and so did Major, who is clearly much more comfortable in relaxed gatherings than making formal set-piece speeches, when his delivery can sound wooden.
He told the anecdote to show the importance of personal relations with world leaders and took the opportunity to wish Yeltsin well for his pending heart surgery.
"I hope that Boris Yeltsin soon successfully has his operation and is fit and can go back to running that country," Major said.
